def write_kml(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    filename: str | os.PathLike,
    *,
    color: str = DEFAULT_KML_COLOR,
    field: str | None = None,
    colormap: str = "rdylbu",
    max_std: float = 3.0,
    value_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    color_classes: int = DEFAULT_COLOR_CLASSES,
    heights: str = "ground",
    height_offset: float = 0.0,
    extrude: bool = False,
    line_width: float = 3.0,
    precision: float = 1e-6,
) -> None:
    """Exports a trajectory to a Google Earth KML file.

    The trajectory is written as a time-stamped track (``gx:Track``): Google Earth shows its path and plays
    it back with the time slider. Optionally, it is colored by a field (speed, height or time).

    Requires the trajectory to have a valid EPSG code so it can be converted to WGS84 (EPSG:4326).

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to export.
        filename (str): The output filename (e.g., "track.kml").
        color (str, optional): Color of the track and its points as "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA", if it is not
            colored by a field. Defaults to red.
        field (str, optional): Key of the field that colors the line:
            "speed", "height" or "time". Defaults to none (one color).
        colormap (str, optional): Color scale of the field:
            "rdylbu" (blue = low, red = high, like the plots) or "viridis" (colorblind-safe). Defaults to "rdylbu".
        max_std (float, optional): The color scale is clipped to mean ± ``max_std`` standard deviations
            (0 = minimum to maximum). Ignored if ``value_range`` is given. Defaults to 3.0, like the plots.
        value_range (tuple[float, float], optional): Fixed (lower, upper) limits of the color scale, e.g. to
            compare several exports; values beyond them get the color of the nearest limit. Defaults to none.
        color_classes (int, optional): Number of colors of the scale. Defaults to 11.
        heights (str, optional): Vertical placement: "ground" (clamped to the
            terrain), "ellipsoidal" (the trajectory's heights are ellipsoidal heights, e.g. GNSS; converted with
            the EGM96 geoid, which needs an internet connection the first time) or "sea_level" (the heights are
            above sea level). Defaults to "ground".
        height_offset (float, optional): Meters added to the heights; with "ground", the trajectory floats
            this far above the terrain. Defaults to 0.
        extrude (bool, optional): Connect the trajectory to the ground with a vertical curtain (not with
            "ground" and no offset). Defaults to False.
        line_width (float, optional): Line width in pixels. Defaults to 3.
        precision (float, optional): Coordinate precision in degrees. Defaults to 1e-6 (about 0.1 m).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the trajectory does not have a known EPSG code, an option is invalid, or the geoid model
            is not available.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.Trajectory.to_kml`][trajectopy.Trajectory.to_kml]: the same as a method.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> from trajectopy import io
        >>> xyz = np.column_stack([364000.0 + np.arange(10.0), np.full(10, 5621000.0), np.full(10, 60.0)])
        >>> track = tpy.Trajectory(tpy.Positions(xyz, epsg=25832), timestamps=np.arange(10.0))
        >>> io.write_kml(track, "track.kml", color="#1f77b4")
    """
    filename = os.fspath(filename)
    scale = _ColorScale(colormap, max_std, value_range, color_classes)
    placement = _placement(trajectory, heights, height_offset)
    root, document = _document(trajectory.name)
    if field is None:
        _add_track_style(document, "track", kml_color(color), line_width)
        _add_track(document, trajectory.name, "track", placement, extrude, precision)
    else:
        selected = _field(trajectory_kml_fields(), field)
        values = np.asarray(selected.values(trajectory), dtype=float)[placement.order]
        _add_colored_line(
            document, trajectory.name, selected, values, placement, scale, extrude, line_width, precision
        )
    _write(root, filename)

        [`trajectopy.ATEResult.to_kml`][trajectopy.ATEResult.to_kml]: the same as a method.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> from trajectopy import io
        >>> t = np.arange(0.0, 100.0)
        >>> xyz = np.column_stack([364000.0 + t, 5621000.0 + np.sin(t / 10), np.full_like(t, 60.0)])
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory(tpy.Positions(xyz, epsg=25832), timestamps=t)
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory(tpy.Positions(xyz + 0.1, epsg=25832), timestamps=t)
        >>> ate_result = tpy.ate(estimate, reference, align=False)
        >>> io.write_ate_kml(ate_result, "ate.kml", field="along_track")
    """
    filename = os.fspath(filename)
    selected = _field(ate_kml_fields(ate_result), field)
    scale = _ColorScale(colormap, max_std, value_range, color_classes)
    placement = _placement(ate_result.trajectory, heights, height_offset)
    values = np.asarray(selected.values(ate_result), dtype=float)[placement.order]
    root, document = _document(ate_result.name)
    _add_colored_line(document, ate_result.name, selected, values, placement, scale, extrude, line_width, precision)
    _write(root, filename)

def estimate_alignment(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    other: Trajectory,
    settings: AlignmentSettings | ProcessingSettings | None = None,
    *,
    initial_parameters: AlignmentParameters | None = None,
) -> AlignmentResult:
    """Estimates the alignment between two trajectories.

    Performs Helmert, Leverarm, and Time shift estimation depending on the configuration.
    This function only estimates the alignment parameters, it does not apply them to the trajectory.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to align.
        other (Trajectory): Reference trajectory to align to.
        settings (AlignmentSettings | ProcessingSettings, optional): Alignment settings, or processing
            settings whose alignment and matching settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.
        initial_parameters (AlignmentParameters, optional): Prior (e.g. from the interactive alignment) used as
            start values of the least squares adjustment instead of the direct initialization. Parameters
            that are not estimated stay fixed at their prior value. A time shift of the prior may be large
            (e.g. trajectories recorded with unrelated clocks): the timestamps are shifted by it before the
            trajectories are matched, and only the remaining time shift is estimated. Defaults to None.

    Returns:
        AlignmentResult: Result of the alignment process.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.apply_alignment`][trajectopy.apply_alignment]: applies the result.
        [`trajectopy.align`][trajectopy.align]: both steps at once.
        [`trajectopy.AlignmentSettings`][trajectopy.AlignmentSettings]: which parameters are estimated.

    References:
        1. G. Tombrink, A. Dreier, L. Klingbeil, H. Kuhlmann (2024): Spatio-temporal trajectory alignment for trajectory evaluation. Journal of Applied Geodesy. https://doi.org/10.1515/jag-2024-0040

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> alignment = tpy.estimate_alignment(estimate, reference)
        >>> alignment.converged
        True
        >>> print(f"{alignment.position_parameters.sim_trans_x.value:.3f} m")
        -1.363 m
        >>> aligned = tpy.apply_alignment(estimate, alignment)
    """
    alignment_settings, matching_settings = _alignment_and_matching_settings(settings)

    logger.info("Aligning trajectory positions ...")

    # The time shift is modelled by the velocity (x + v * dt), which only holds for small shifts. A prior time
    # shift is therefore applied to the timestamps beforehand and added to the estimated (remaining) one.
    prior_time_shift = 0.0 if initial_parameters is None else float(initial_parameters.time_shift.value)
    if initial_parameters is not None and prior_time_shift != 0.0:
        trajectory = trajectory.copy()
        trajectory.timestamps = trajectory.timestamps - prior_time_shift
        initial_parameters = copy.deepcopy(initial_parameters)
        initial_parameters.time_shift.value = 0.0
        initial_parameters.time_shift.default = 0.0

    alignment_data = AlignmentData(
        traj_from=trajectory,
        traj_to=other,
        alignment_settings=alignment_settings,
        matching_settings=matching_settings,
    )
    ghm_alignment = AlignmentEstimator(alignment_data=alignment_data, initial_parameters=initial_parameters)
    estimated_parameters = ghm_alignment.estimate_parameters()
    if prior_time_shift != 0.0:
        time_shift = estimated_parameters.time_shift
        time_shift.value = time_shift.value + prior_time_shift
        time_shift.default = time_shift.default + prior_time_shift

    pre_aligned_rotations = (
        alignment_data.traj_from.transform(estimated_parameters.sim3_matrix, inplace=False).rotations
        if alignment_settings.estimation_settings.sensor_rotation
        else None
    )
    if pre_aligned_rotations is not None and alignment_data.traj_to.rotations is not None:
        logger.info("Aligning rotations ...")
        sensor_rot_params = align_rotations(rot_from=pre_aligned_rotations, rot_to=alignment_data.traj_to.rotations)
        logger.info("Estimated sensor rotation:\n%s", sensor_rot_params)
    else:
        sensor_rot_params = SensorRotationParameters(enabled=False)

    return AlignmentResult(
        name=f"{alignment_data.traj_from.name} to {alignment_data.traj_to.name}",
        position_parameters=estimated_parameters,
        rotation_parameters=sensor_rot_params,
        estimation_of=ghm_alignment.settings.estimation_settings,
        # without least squares parameters there is nothing that could fail to converge
        converged=ghm_alignment.has_results or alignment_settings.estimation_settings.all_lq_disabled,
    )

Transforms trajectory using alignment parameters.

After computing the alignment parameters needed to align two trajectories, they can be applied to arbitrary trajectories.

Parameters:

Examples:

>>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")

def apply_alignment(
    trajectory: Trajectory, alignment_result: AlignmentResult, *, inplace: bool = False
) -> "Trajectory":
    """Transforms trajectory using alignment parameters.

    After computing the alignment parameters needed to align two trajectories, they can be
    applied to arbitrary trajectories.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to apply alignment to.
        alignment_result (AlignmentResult): Alignment result containing transformation parameters.
        inplace (bool, optional): Perform in-place. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Aligned trajectory.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.estimate_alignment`][trajectopy.estimate_alignment]: estimates the alignment.
        [`trajectopy.align`][trajectopy.align]: both steps at once.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> alignment = tpy.estimate_alignment(estimate, reference)
        >>> aligned = tpy.apply_alignment(estimate, alignment)
        >>> len(aligned) == len(estimate)
        True
    """

    def _prepare_alignment_application(
        trajectory: Trajectory, alignment_parameters: AlignmentParameters
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float, float, float]:
        if trajectory.rotations is not None:
            rpy = trajectory.rotations.as_euler("xyz", degrees=False)
            euler_x, euler_y, euler_z = rpy[:, 0], rpy[:, 1], rpy[:, 2]
            lever_x, lever_y, lever_z = (
                alignment_parameters.lever_x.value,
                alignment_parameters.lever_y.value,
                alignment_parameters.lever_z.value,
            )
        else:
            if any(
                parameter.value != 0.0
                for parameter in (
                    alignment_parameters.lever_x,
                    alignment_parameters.lever_y,
                    alignment_parameters.lever_z,
                )
            ):
                logger.warning("Trajectory has no orientations. Cannot apply leverarm.")
            euler_x = euler_y = euler_z = np.zeros(len(trajectory))
            lever_x, lever_y, lever_z = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0

        return euler_x, euler_y, euler_z, lever_x, lever_y, lever_z

    trajectory = trajectory if inplace else trajectory.copy()
    has_orientations = trajectory.has_orientation

    # leverarm and time
    (
        euler_x,
        euler_y,
        euler_z,
        lever_x,
        lever_y,
        lever_z,
    ) = _prepare_alignment_application(trajectory, alignment_result.position_parameters)

    # do not use velocities for time shift application
    trafo_x, trafo_y, trafo_z = leverarm_time_component(
        euler_x=euler_x,
        euler_y=euler_y,
        euler_z=euler_z,
        lever_x=lever_x,
        lever_y=lever_y,
        lever_z=lever_z,
        time_shift=0,
        speed_x=0,
        speed_y=0,
        speed_z=0,
    )
    trajectory.positions.xyz += np.c_[trafo_x, trafo_y, trafo_z]

    # instead, apply time shift as a simple shift of the timestamps
    trajectory.timestamps -= alignment_result.position_parameters.time_shift.value
    logger.info(
        f"Applied time shift of {alignment_result.position_parameters.time_shift.value * 1000:.1f} ms to timestamps."
    )

    # similiarity transformation
    trajectory.transform(alignment_result.position_parameters.sim3_matrix, inplace=True)

    logger.info("Applied alignment parameters to positions.")

    # sensor orientation (mounting rotation in the body frame)
    if trajectory.rotations is not None:
        trajectory.rotations = trajectory.rotations * alignment_result.rotation_parameters.rotation_set
        logger.info("Applied alignment parameters to orientations.")

    if not has_orientations:
        trajectory.rotations = None

    return trajectory

def align(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    other: Trajectory,
    settings: AlignmentSettings | ProcessingSettings | None = None,
    *,
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Aligns the trajectory with another trajectory.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to align.
        other (Trajectory): Reference trajectory.
        settings (AlignmentSettings | ProcessingSettings, optional): Alignment settings, or processing
            settings whose alignment and matching settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.
        inplace (bool, optional): Perform in-place. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Aligned trajectory.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.estimate_alignment`][trajectopy.estimate_alignment], [`trajectopy.apply_alignment`][trajectopy.apply_alignment]: the single steps.

    References:
        1. G. Tombrink, A. Dreier, L. Klingbeil, H. Kuhlmann (2024): Spatio-temporal trajectory alignment for trajectory evaluation. Journal of Applied Geodesy. https://doi.org/10.1515/jag-2024-0040

        True
    """
    alignment = estimate_alignment(trajectory, other, settings)
    return apply_alignment(trajectory=trajectory, alignment_result=alignment, inplace=inplace)

match_trajectories(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    other: Trajectory,
    settings: MatchingSettings
    | ProcessingSettings
    | None = None,
    *,
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Trajectory, Trajectory]

Matches two trajectories using the specified method.

Supported methods:

  • INTERPOLATION: Interpolates the test trajectory onto the reference trajectory using its timestamps. The interpolation is linear for both positions and rotations (SLERP).
  • NEAREST_TEMPORAL: Finds the nearest temporal match without interpolation by finding the nearest timestamp in the target trajectory for each timestamp in the source trajectory.
  • NEAREST_SPATIAL: Finds the nearest spatial match without interpolation by finding the nearest pose in the target trajectory for each pose in the source trajectory using Euclidean distance.
  • NEAREST_SPATIAL_INTERPOLATED: Finds the nearest k spatial matches and spatially interpolates using a 3d line; the orientations of the reference are averaged over the same nearest poses, the trajectory keeps its own. Both trajectories will have the length of the test trajectory.

Parameters:

  • trajectory (Trajectory) –

    Trajectory to match.

  • other (Trajectory) –

    Other trajectory to match against.

  • settings (MatchingSettings | ProcessingSettings, default: None ) –

    Matching settings, or processing settings whose matching settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.

  • inplace (bool, default: False ) –

    Whether to modify the input trajectories. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • tuple[Trajectory, Trajectory] –

    Tuple[Trajectory, Trajectory]: Matched trajectories.

See Also

trajectopy.MatchingSettings: the methods. trajectopy.interpolate: interpolation at given timestamps.

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
>>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
>>> matched, matched_reference = tpy.match_trajectories(
...     estimate, reference, tpy.MatchingSettings(method="nearest_temporal")
... )
>>> len(matched) == len(matched_reference)
True

def match_trajectories(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    other: Trajectory,
    settings: MatchingSettings | ProcessingSettings | None = None,
    *,
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Trajectory, Trajectory]:
    """Matches two trajectories using the specified method.

    Supported methods:

    - **INTERPOLATION**: Interpolates the test trajectory onto the reference trajectory using
      its timestamps. The interpolation is linear for both positions and rotations (SLERP).
    - **NEAREST_TEMPORAL**: Finds the nearest temporal match without interpolation by finding
      the nearest timestamp in the target trajectory for each timestamp in the source trajectory.
    - **NEAREST_SPATIAL**: Finds the nearest spatial match without interpolation by finding
      the nearest pose in the target trajectory for each pose in the source trajectory using
      Euclidean distance.
    - **NEAREST_SPATIAL_INTERPOLATED**: Finds the nearest k spatial matches and spatially
      interpolates using a 3d line; the orientations of the reference are averaged over the same nearest
      poses, the trajectory keeps its own. Both trajectories will have the length of the test trajectory.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to match.
        other (Trajectory): Other trajectory to match against.
        settings (MatchingSettings | ProcessingSettings, optional): Matching settings, or processing settings
            whose matching settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.
        inplace (bool, optional): Whether to modify the input trajectories. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Tuple[Trajectory, Trajectory]: Matched trajectories.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.MatchingSettings`][trajectopy.MatchingSettings]: the methods.
        [`trajectopy.interpolate`][trajectopy.interpolate]: interpolation at given timestamps.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> matched, matched_reference = tpy.match_trajectories(
        ...     estimate, reference, tpy.MatchingSettings(method="nearest_temporal")
        ... )
        >>> len(matched) == len(matched_reference)
        True
    """
    matching_settings = resolve_settings(settings, MatchingSettings)

    trajectory = trajectory if inplace else trajectory.copy()
    other = other if inplace else other.copy()

    if (
        trajectory.sorting == Sorting.PATH_LENGTH
        and other.sorting == Sorting.PATH_LENGTH
        and matching_settings.method in [MatchingMethod.NEAREST_TEMPORAL, MatchingMethod.INTERPOLATION]
        and not np.array_equal(trajectory.index, other.index)
    ):
        _adopt_reference_path_lengths(trajectory=trajectory, other=other)

    if not trajectory.overlaps_with(other) and matching_settings.method in [
        MatchingMethod.NEAREST_TEMPORAL,
        MatchingMethod.INTERPOLATION,
    ]:
        logger.warning("Trajectories do not overlap! Performing rough matching first.")
        timeshift = match_non_overlapping_stamps(
            trajectory=other, other=trajectory, max_distance=matching_settings.max_distance
        )
        logger.info("Rough matching index offset: %.3f", timeshift)

        if trajectory.sorting == Sorting.TIME:
            trajectory.timestamps = trajectory.timestamps + timeshift
        else:
            trajectory.path_lengths = trajectory.path_lengths + timeshift

    logger.info("Matching trajectories using method %s", matching_settings.method.name)

    if matching_settings.method == MatchingMethod.INTERPOLATION:
        return _match_trajectories_interpolation(
            trajectory=trajectory, other=other, max_gap_size=matching_settings.max_gap_size
        )

    if matching_settings.method == MatchingMethod.NEAREST_TEMPORAL:
        return _match_trajectories_temporal(
            trajectory=trajectory, other=other, max_distance=matching_settings.max_time_diff
        )

    if matching_settings.method == MatchingMethod.NEAREST_SPATIAL:
        return _match_trajectories_spatial(
            trajectory=trajectory, other=other, max_distance=matching_settings.max_distance
        )

    if matching_settings.method == MatchingMethod.NEAREST_SPATIAL_INTERPOLATED:
        return _match_trajectories_spatial_interpolation(
            trajectory=trajectory,
            other=other,
            max_distance=matching_settings.max_distance,
            k_nearest=matching_settings.k_nearest,
        )

    raise ValueError(f"Matching method {matching_settings.method} not supported!")

Interpolates a trajectory to specified timestamps using the given method.

The index is sorted first. Values outside the index range of the trajectory (which would need an extrapolation) and inside gaps larger than max_gap_size are left out, so the result can have fewer poses than index.

Parameters:

  • index (ArrayLike) –

    Interpolation index (timestamps or path lengths, depending on the sorting).

  • method (InterpolationMethod | str, default: LINEAR ) –

    Interpolation method. Defaults to "linear".

  • max_gap_size (float, default: float('inf') ) –

    Maximum gap in the index over which to interpolate. Defaults to infinity.

  • inplace (bool, default: False ) –

    Perform in-place interpolation. Defaults to False.

Returns:

    Interpolated trajectory

Raises:

    If the trajectory is empty, no value of index lies within its range or the method is not supported.

Examples:

def interpolate(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    index: ArrayLike,
    *,
    method: InterpolationMethod | str = InterpolationMethod.LINEAR,
    max_gap_size: float = float("inf"),
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> "Trajectory":
    """Interpolates a trajectory to specified timestamps using the given method.

    The index is sorted first. Values outside the index range of the trajectory (which would need an
    extrapolation) and inside gaps larger than ``max_gap_size`` are left out, so the result can have fewer poses
    than ``index``.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to interpolate
        index (ArrayLike): Interpolation index (timestamps or path lengths, depending on the sorting).
        method (InterpolationMethod | str, optional): Interpolation method. Defaults to ``"linear"``.
        max_gap_size (float, optional): Maximum gap in the index over which to interpolate. Defaults to infinity.
        inplace (bool, optional): Perform in-place interpolation. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Interpolated trajectory

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the trajectory is empty, no value of ``index`` lies within its range or the method is
            not supported.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.match_trajectories`][trajectopy.match_trajectories]: interpolation at the timestamps of a reference.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> tpy.interpolate(reference, [0.5, 1.5]).timestamps
        array([0.5, 1.5])
    """
    if InterpolationMethod(method) == InterpolationMethod.LINEAR:
        return _interpolate_linear(trajectory, np.asarray(index, dtype=float), inplace, max_gap_size)
    raise ValueError(f"Interpolation method '{method}' is not supported.")

>>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")

def approximate(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    settings: ApproximationSettings | ProcessingSettings | None = None,
    *,
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Approximate the trajectory using piecewise cubic polynomials based on the provided settings.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): The trajectory to approximate.
        settings (ApproximationSettings | ProcessingSettings, optional): Approximation settings, or processing
            settings whose approximation settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.
        inplace (bool): If True, modify the trajectory in place. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: The approximated trajectory.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.ApproximationSettings`][trajectopy.ApproximationSettings]: the options.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> smoothed = tpy.approximate(reference, tpy.ApproximationSettings(position_interval_size=50.0))
        >>> len(smoothed) == len(reference)
        True
    """
    approximation_settings = resolve_settings(settings, ApproximationSettings)

    if approximation_settings.position_approximation_method == PositionApproximationMethod.CUBIC:
        xyz_approx = _piecewise_cubic(
            index=trajectory.index,
            values=trajectory.xyz,
            min_win_size=approximation_settings.position_interval_size,
            min_obs=approximation_settings.position_min_observations,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown position approximation method: {approximation_settings.position_approximation_method}"
        )

    traj_approx = trajectory if inplace else trajectory.copy()
    traj_approx.positions.xyz = xyz_approx

    if not traj_approx.has_orientation:
        return traj_approx

    if approximation_settings.rotation_approximation_method == RotationApproximationMethod.AVERAGE_PER_PATH_LENGTH:
        quat_approx = _average_rotations_per_path_length(
            trajectory, max_gap_size=approximation_settings.max_path_length_gap
        )
    elif approximation_settings.rotation_approximation_method == RotationApproximationMethod.AVERAGE_IN_WINDOW:
        quat_approx = _average_rotations_in_window(
            index=trajectory.index,
            quat=trajectory.quat,
            win_size=approximation_settings.rotation_window_size,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown rotation approximation method: {approximation_settings.rotation_approximation_method}"
        )
    traj_approx.rotations = Rotation.from_quat(quat_approx)

    return traj_approx

def sort_spatially(
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    settings: SortingSettings | ProcessingSettings | None = None,
    *,
    inplace: bool = False,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Sorts the trajectory spatially. This is only useful for trajectories
    that describe a closed loop without intersections.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory to sort.
        settings (SortingSettings | ProcessingSettings, optional): Sorting settings, or processing settings
            whose sorting settings are used. Defaults to the default settings.
        inplace (bool, optional): Whether to sort the trajectory in-place. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Sorted trajectory.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.divide_into_laps`][trajectopy.divide_into_laps]: splits a sorted trajectory into laps.
        [`trajectopy.SortingSettings`][trajectopy.SortingSettings]: the options.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> angle = np.linspace(0.0, 4 * np.pi, 400)  # two laps
        >>> loop = tpy.Trajectory(np.column_stack([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0 * angle]))
        >>> tpy.sort_spatially(loop).sorting
        <Sorting.PATH_LENGTH: 'path_length'>
    """
    sort_idx, arc_lengths = _sort_xyz(
        xyz=trajectory.positions.xyz, settings=resolve_settings(settings, SortingSettings)
    )
    trajectory = trajectory.mask(sort_idx, inplace=inplace)
    trajectory.path_lengths = arc_lengths
    trajectory.set_sorting(Sorting.PATH_LENGTH)
    return trajectory

def divide_into_laps(
    trajectory: Trajectory, *, return_lap_indices: bool = False
) -> list[Trajectory] | tuple[list[Trajectory], np.ndarray]:
    """Divides a spatially sorted trajectory into laps.

    This is only useful for trajectories that describe a closed loop without intersections. A new lap starts
    where the path length of the spatially sorted trajectory jumps back to the start of the loop.

    Args:
        trajectory (Trajectory): Trajectory sorted by path length (see [`sort_spatially`][trajectopy.sort_spatially]).
        return_lap_indices (bool, optional): Whether to return lap indices. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        list[Trajectory] | tuple[list[Trajectory], np.ndarray]: The laps, each sorted by path length. With
        ``return_lap_indices=True``, a tuple of the laps and the indices of the chronologically ordered
        trajectory at which the laps start (followed by the number of poses).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the trajectory is not sorted by path length.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.sort_spatially`][trajectopy.sort_spatially]: sorts a trajectory spatially first.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> angle = np.linspace(0.0, 4 * np.pi, 400, endpoint=False)  # two laps
        >>> loop = tpy.sort_spatially(tpy.Trajectory(np.column_stack([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0 * angle])))
        >>> len(tpy.divide_into_laps(loop))
        2
    """
    if trajectory.sorting != Sorting.PATH_LENGTH:
        logger.error("Provide a trajectory sorted by path length to divide into laps.")
        raise ValueError("Trajectory must be sorted by path length to divide into laps.")
    else:
        trajectory = trajectory.copy()

    trajectory.set_sorting(Sorting.TIME)
    arc_length_diffs = np.diff(trajectory.path_lengths)
    arc_length_threshold = 0.95 * np.max(trajectory.path_lengths)
    lap_indices = np.r_[0, np.where(np.abs(arc_length_diffs) > arc_length_threshold)[0], len(trajectory)]

    # divide into laps
    laps = []
    for i in range(len(lap_indices) - 1):
        lap = trajectory.mask(np.arange(lap_indices[i], lap_indices[i + 1]), inplace=False)
        lap.set_sorting(Sorting.PATH_LENGTH)
        laps.append(lap)

    return laps if (not return_lap_indices) else (laps, lap_indices)

def merge_trajectories(trajectories: Iterable[Trajectory]) -> Trajectory:
    """Merges a list of trajectories into one trajectory.

    This function ignores EPSG codes and merges the trajectories based on their timestamps.
    Therefore, all trajectories should be in the same coordinate system before merging.

    Args:
        trajectories (Iterable[Trajectory]): List of trajectories to merge.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Merged trajectory.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no trajectories are provided.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.average_trajectories`][trajectopy.average_trajectories]: pose-wise mean instead.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> merged = tpy.merge_trajectories([reference.crop(0.0, 9.0), reference.crop(10.0, 19.0)])
        >>> len(merged)
        20
    """
    trajectories = list(trajectories)
    if not trajectories:
        raise ValueError("Cannot merge empty list of trajectories")

    epsg_set = {t.positions.epsg for t in trajectories}

    if len(epsg_set) > 1:
        logger.warning(
            "Merging trajectories with different EPSG codes. "
            "This may lead to unexpected results. "
            "Consider reprojecting the trajectories to the same EPSG code."
        )

    epsg = trajectories[0].positions.epsg  # the first trajectory's, not an arbitrary one of the set

    merged_xyz = np.concatenate([t.positions.xyz for t in trajectories], axis=0)
    # orientations only if all trajectories have them: any substitute would be made-up data
    with_orientation = all(t.rotations is not None for t in trajectories)
    if not with_orientation and any(t.rotations is not None for t in trajectories):
        logger.warning("Not all merged trajectories have orientations. The merged trajectory has none.")
    merged_rotations = (
        Rotation.from_quat(np.concatenate([t.quat for t in trajectories], axis=0)) if with_orientation else None
    )
    merged_timestamps = np.concatenate([t.timestamps for t in trajectories], axis=0)
    merged_velocities = np.concatenate([t.velocity_xyz for t in trajectories], axis=0)
    merged_std = (
        np.concatenate([t.position_std for t in trajectories if t.position_std is not None], axis=0)
        if all(t.position_std is not None for t in trajectories)
        else None
    )

    # the trajectory orders the poses chronologically before it derives the path lengths
    return Trajectory(
        name="Merged",
        timestamps=merged_timestamps,
        positions=Positions(xyz=merged_xyz, epsg=epsg),
        rotations=merged_rotations,
        velocity_xyz=merged_velocities,
        position_std=merged_std,
    )

def average_trajectories(trajectories: Iterable[Trajectory]) -> Trajectory:
    """Averages a list of trajectories into one trajectory.

    This function ignores EPSG codes and averages trajectories.

    Args:
        trajectories (Iterable[Trajectory]): List of trajectories to average.

    Returns:
        Trajectory: Averaged trajectory.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If trajectories have different lengths or no trajectories provided.

    See Also:
        [`trajectopy.merge_trajectories`][trajectopy.merge_trajectories]: concatenates trajectories instead.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> averaged = tpy.average_trajectories([reference, reference.copy()])
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> np.allclose(averaged.xyz, reference.xyz)
        True
    """
    trajectories = list(trajectories)
    if not trajectories:
        raise ValueError("Cannot average empty list of trajectories")

    lengths = {len(t) for t in trajectories}

    if len(lengths) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "Trajectories must have the same length to be averaged. Ensure this using trajectory matching."
        )

    xyz_stack = np.stack([t.positions.xyz for t in trajectories], axis=0)

    rots = [t.rotations.as_quat() for t in trajectories if t.rotations is not None]
    mean_rots = []
    for i in range(len(trajectories[0])):
        rotations = [rot[i] for rot in rots]
        if not rotations:
            continue

        mean_rots.append(Rotation.from_quat(np.array(rotations)).mean().as_quat())

    avg_xyz = np.mean(xyz_stack, axis=0)

    return Trajectory(
        name="Averaged",
        timestamps=trajectories[0].timestamps,
        positions=Positions(xyz=avg_xyz, epsg=trajectories[0].positions.epsg),
        rotations=Rotation.from_quat(np.array(mean_rots)) if mean_rots else None,
    )

def describe(self) -> pd.Series:
    """Statistics of the deviations, like `pandas.DataFrame.describe`.

    Position statistics are in meters, rotation statistics in radians; rotation statistics are NaN
    without orientations. ``pos_mean`` is the position ATE, ``rot_mean`` the rotation ATE.

    Returns:
        pd.Series: Statistics, named after the result.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> ate_result = tpy.ate(estimate, reference)
        >>> ate_result.describe()[["poses", "pos_mean", "pos_rms"]].round(3)
        poses       4541.000
        pos_mean       1.153
        pos_rms        1.304
        Name: KITTI ORB vs. KITTI Ground Truth, dtype: float64
    """
    statistics: dict[str, float] = {
        "poses": float(len(self)),
        "pos_mean": float(self.pos_ate),
        "pos_median": float(self.pos_dev_median),
        "pos_rms": float(self.pos_dev_rms),
        "pos_std": float(self.pos_dev_std),
        "pos_p95": float(self.pos_dev_p95),
        "pos_min": float(self.pos_dev_min),
        "pos_max": float(self.pos_dev_max),
        "pos_bias_x": float(self.pos_bias_x),
        "pos_bias_y": float(self.pos_bias_y),
        "pos_bias_z": float(self.pos_bias_z),
        "pos_bias_along": float(self.pos_bias_along),
        "pos_bias_cross_h": float(self.pos_bias_cross_h),
        "pos_bias_cross_v": float(self.pos_bias_cross_v),
    }
    rotation_keys = ("rot_mean", "rot_rms", "rot_std", "rot_p95", "rot_max")
    if self.has_orientation:
        values = (self.rot_ate, self.rot_dev_rms, self.rot_dev_std, self.rot_dev_p95, self.rot_dev_max)
        statistics |= {key: float(value) for key, value in zip(rotation_keys, values)}
    else:
        statistics |= dict.fromkeys(rotation_keys, np.nan)
    return pd.Series(statistics, name=self.name)

def remove_ate_above(self, threshold: float) -> None:
    """Removes the deviations (and their poses) whose position deviation is not below a threshold.

    This is useful to remove outliers from the ATE.

    Args:
        threshold (float): Deviations of this size (m) and larger are removed; 0 or less keeps all.
    """
    if threshold <= 0.0:
        return

    ate_below_idx = self.pos_dev_comb < threshold
    self.trajectory.mask(ate_below_idx, inplace=True)

    self.abs_dev.pos_dev = self.abs_dev.pos_dev[ate_below_idx]
    self.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev = self.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev[ate_below_idx]

    if self.abs_dev.rot_dev is not None:
        # selected as quaternions, a round trip through Euler angles is inexact near gimbal lock
        self.abs_dev.rot_dev = self.abs_dev.rot_dev[ate_below_idx]

    # the combined deviations and rotation statistics are cached and depend on the removed deviations
    for cached in _CACHED:
        self.__dict__.pop(cached, None)

confidence_interval(
    *,
    quantity: str = "position",
    statistic: str = "mean",
    confidence: float = DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE,

Confidence interval of the mean (ATE) or RMS of the position or rotation deviations.

The deviations are usually correlated in time, so that the interval is derived with a moving block bootstrap whose blocks are twice as long as the correlation time. It describes how precisely the deviations of this evaluation determine the statistic, e.g. whether two estimates differ significantly. It is reproducible (fixed seed) and cached.

Parameters:

  • quantity (str, default: 'position' ) –

    position (meters) or rotation (radians), case-insensitive. Defaults to position.

  • statistic (str, default: 'mean' ) –

    mean or rms, case-insensitive. Defaults to mean.

  • confidence (float, default: DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE ) –

    Confidence level. Defaults to 0.95.

Returns:

  • tuple[float, float] –

    tuple[float, float]: Lower and upper bound.

References
  1. H. R. Künsch (1989): The jackknife and the bootstrap for general stationary observations. The Annals of Statistics 17(3), 1217-1241.
Source code in trajectopy\results\ate_result.py 
def confidence_interval(
    self, *, quantity: str = "position", statistic: str = "mean", confidence: float = DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Confidence interval of the mean (ATE) or RMS of the position or rotation deviations.

    The deviations are usually correlated in time, so that the interval is derived with a moving block
    bootstrap whose blocks are twice as long as the correlation time. It describes how precisely the
    deviations of this evaluation determine the statistic, e.g. whether two estimates differ significantly. It is
    reproducible (fixed seed) and cached.

    Args:
        quantity (str, optional): ``position`` (meters) or ``rotation`` (radians), case-insensitive.
            Defaults to ``position``.
        statistic (str, optional): ``mean`` or ``rms``, case-insensitive. Defaults to ``mean``.
        confidence (float, optional): Confidence level. Defaults to 0.95.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float]: Lower and upper bound.

    References:
        1. H. R. Künsch (1989): The jackknife and the bootstrap for general stationary observations. The Annals of Statistics 17(3), 1217-1241.
    """
    quantity, statistic = quantity.lower(), statistic.lower()
    if quantity not in ("position", "rotation"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown quantity '{quantity}', use 'position' or 'rotation'.")
    if statistic not in ("mean", "rms"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown statistic '{statistic}', use 'mean' or 'rms'.")
    key = (quantity, statistic, confidence)
    if key not in self._confidence_intervals:
        values = self.pos_dev_comb if quantity == "position" else self.rot_dev_comb
        order = np.argsort(self.trajectory.timestamps, kind="stable")  # chronological, also if sorted spatially
        self._confidence_intervals[key] = block_bootstrap_ci(
            values[order], self.trajectory.timestamps[order], statistic=statistic, confidence=confidence
        )
    return self._confidence_intervals[key]

def segment_statistics(
    self,
    *,
    segment_length: float | None = None,
    by: str = "time",
    labels: np.ndarray | list | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Statistics of the deviations in segments of the trajectory, e.g. to compare sections of different
    conditions (tunnel and open sky) or to see whether the accuracy changes over time.

    Segments are either consecutive windows of ``segment_length`` seconds (``by="time"``) or meters
    (``by="path_length"``), or given by a label of each deviation (``labels``, e.g. from a classification of
    the environment).

    Args:
        segment_length (float | None, optional): Length of the windows. Required unless labels are given.
        by (str, optional): ``time`` or ``path_length``. Defaults to ``time``.
        labels (np.ndarray | list | None, optional): Segment label of each deviation (in the current order of
            the result). Overrides segment_length.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: One row per segment with the columns ``segment``, ``start`` and ``end`` (smallest and
        largest time or path length), ``count``, ``pos_mean``, ``pos_median``, ``pos_rms``, ``pos_p95``,
        ``pos_max`` (meters) and, with orientations, ``rot_mean``, ``rot_rms`` and ``rot_max`` (degrees).
    """
    by = by.lower()
    if by not in ("time", "path_length"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown segment index '{by}', use 'time' or 'path_length'.")
    index = self.trajectory.timestamps if by == "time" else self.trajectory.path_lengths
    if labels is not None:
        segment = np.asarray(labels)
        if len(segment) != len(self.pos_dev_comb):
            raise ValueError(f"{len(segment)} labels were given for {len(self.pos_dev_comb)} deviations.")
    elif segment_length is not None:
        segment = segment_ids(index, segment_length)
    else:
        raise ValueError("Give either a segment length or labels.")

    frame = pd.DataFrame({"segment": segment, "index": index, "pos": self.pos_dev_comb})
    if self.has_orientation:
        frame["rot"] = np.rad2deg(self.rot_dev_comb)

    def p95(values: pd.Series) -> float:
        return float(np.percentile(values, 95))

    def rms_of(values: pd.Series) -> float:
        return float(rms(values.to_numpy()))

    grouped = frame.groupby("segment", sort=True)
    table = grouped.agg(
        start=("index", "min"),
        end=("index", "max"),
        count=("pos", "size"),
        pos_mean=("pos", "mean"),
        pos_median=("pos", "median"),
        pos_rms=("pos", rms_of),
        pos_p95=("pos", p95),
        pos_max=("pos", "max"),
    )
    if self.has_orientation:
        table = table.join(grouped.agg(rot_mean=("rot", "mean"), rot_rms=("rot", rms_of), rot_max=("rot", "max")))
    return table.reset_index()

def set_sorting(self, sorting: Sorting | str) -> None:
    """Orders the trajectory and its deviations by time or path length.

    Args:
        sorting (Sorting | str): New sorting.
    """
    sorting = Sorting(sorting)
    if sorting == self.trajectory.sorting:
        return

    order = self.trajectory.sort_index(sorting)
    self.trajectory.set_sorting(sorting)

    self.abs_dev.pos_dev = self.abs_dev.pos_dev[order]
    self.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev = self.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev[order]
    if self.abs_dev.rot_dev is not None:
        self.abs_dev.rot_dev = self.abs_dev.rot_dev[order]

    # cached per-epoch deviations follow the old order
    for cached in _CACHED:
        self.__dict__.pop(cached, None)

def to_dataframe(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the deviations of all poses as a table.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: One row per pose: ``time`` [s], ``arc_lengths`` (path length) [m], the position
        ``pos_x/y/z`` and, with orientations, the orientation ``rot_x/y/z/w`` (quaternion) of the evaluated
        trajectory, followed by the deviations (test minus reference) ``pos_dev_x/y/z`` and
        ``pos_dev_along/cross_h/cross_v`` [m] and, with orientations, the deviation rotation
        ``rot_dev_x/y/z/w`` (quaternion).
    """
    trajectory_data = np.c_[
        self.trajectory.timestamps,
        self.trajectory.path_lengths,
        self.trajectory.positions.xyz,
    ]

    if self.trajectory.rotations is not None:
        trajectory_data = np.c_[trajectory_data, self.trajectory.rotations.as_quat()]

    deviation_data = np.c_[self.abs_dev.pos_dev, self.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev]

    if self.abs_dev.rot_dev:
        deviation_data = np.c_[deviation_data, self.abs_dev.rot_dev.as_quat()]

    all_data = np.c_[trajectory_data, deviation_data]

    return pd.DataFrame(all_data, columns=self.columns)

docs.title: AbsoluteTrajectoryDeviations dataclass
docs.text:
AbsoluteTrajectoryDeviations(
    pos_dev: ndarray,
    directed_pos_dev: ndarray,
    rot_dev: Rotation | None = None,
    rotations_used: bool = False,
)

Container holding absolute pose deviations between two trajectories.

The arrays stored in this dataclass represent per-epoch deviations after an optional temporal/spatial alignment of a reference (ground truth) and a test trajectory. They are later aggregated by ATEResult to derive metrics such as mean/median Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE), directional bias, and RMS statistics.

All deviations describe how far the evaluated (test) trajectory deviates from the reference, i.e. test minus reference: a positive x deviation means the test trajectory is further in x direction, a positive along-track deviation that it is ahead, a positive horizontal cross-track deviation that it is to the right and a positive vertical cross-track deviation that it is above.

Attributes:

  • pos_dev (ndarray) –

    3D array of absolute position deviation vectors in meters. Shape is (N, 3) for N deviation vectors with x, y, z components. These deviations are directly depending on the definition of the coordinate frame of the trajectories.

  • directed_pos_dev (ndarray) –

    3D array of directed position deviation vectors (e.g. along-track, horizontal/vertical cross-track) in meters. Shape is (N, 3). These deviations are independent of the global coordinate frame, as they are derived based on the along-track direction of the trajectory.

  • rot_dev (Rotation | None) –

    Optional orientation deviations represented as a scipy Rotation (radians), the rotation from the reference to the test orientation (test * reference^-1). None if rotational evaluation was not performed.

  • rotations_used (bool) –

    Indicates whether trajectory rotation information was employed to derive the direction frame for directed_pos_dev. If False, directional decomposition has relied on positional differences only.

Examples:

import trajectopy as tpy reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj") estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj") abs_dev = tpy.ate(estimate, reference).abs_dev abs_dev.pos_dev.shape, abs_dev.directed_pos_dev.shape ((4541, 3), (4541, 3))

def describe(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Statistics of the drift per pair distance, like `pandas.DataFrame.describe`.

    Position drifts are in % (pairs by distance) or m/s (pairs by time), rotation drifts in rad/100m or
    rad/s; rotation statistics are NaN without orientations.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: One row per pair distance, indexed by the mean distance of the pairs.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> rpe_result = tpy.rpe(estimate, reference)
        >>> table = rpe_result.describe()
        >>> table.index.name, len(table)
        ('pair_distance [m]', 8)
    """
    columns: dict[str, list] = {
        "pairs": self.num_pairs,
        "pos_mean": self.pos_dev_mean,
        "pos_median": self.pos_dev_median,
        "pos_std": self.pos_std,
        "pos_min": self.pos_dev_min,
        "pos_max": self.pos_dev_max,
    }
    rotation = {
        "rot_mean": self.rot_dev_mean,
        "rot_median": self.rot_dev_median,
        "rot_std": self.rot_std,
        "rot_min": self.rot_dev_min,
        "rot_max": self.rot_dev_max,
    }
    for key, values in rotation.items():
        columns[key] = values if self.has_rot_dev else [np.nan] * len(self.num_pairs)
    index = pd.Index(self.mean_pair_distances, name=f"pair_distance [{self.pair_distance_unit}]")
    return pd.DataFrame(columns, index=index)

def compute_metric(self, key: str, func: Callable[[Any], float], *, factor: float = 1.0) -> list[float]:
    """Applies a statistic to the deviations of each pair distance.

    Args:
        key (str): ``"pos_dev"``, ``"rot_dev"`` or ``"pair_distance"``.
        func (Callable): Statistic of an array, e.g. `numpy.mean`.
        factor (float, optional): Factor applied to the statistic, e.g. [`drift_factor`][trajectopy.RPEResult.drift_factor].
            Defaults to 1.

    Returns:
        list[float]: One value per pair distance with deviations.
    """
    return [float(func(values) * factor) for values in self.rpe_dev.__dict__[key].values() if len(values)]

def get_all(self, key: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns the values of all pose pairs of one quantity, concatenated over the pair distances.

    Args:
        key (str): ``"pos_dev"``, ``"rot_dev"`` or ``"pair_distance"``.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: The values as stored (relative deviations, not multiplied by [`drift_factor`][trajectopy.RPEResult.drift_factor]);
        empty if there are none.
    """
    model_dict = self.rpe_dev.__dict__
    if key not in model_dict or not model_dict[key]:
        return np.array([])
    return np.concatenate([np.asarray(values, dtype=float) for values in model_dict[key].values()])

def to_dataframe(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the deviations of all pose pairs as a table.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Columns ``pair_distance`` (m or s), ``pos_dev`` (m/m or m/s) and, with orientations,
        ``rot_dev`` (rad/m or rad/s); one row per pose pair.

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
        >>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
        >>> rpe_result = tpy.rpe(estimate, reference)
        >>> rpe_result.to_dataframe().columns.tolist()
        ['pair_distance', 'pos_dev', 'rot_dev']
    """
    if self.has_rot_dev:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            np.c_[self.all_pair_distances, self.pos_dev_all, self.all_rot_devs], columns=self.columns
        )
    else:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.c_[self.all_pair_distances, self.pos_dev_all], columns=self.columns)

    pos_dev: dict[float, ndarray],
    rot_dev: dict[float, ndarray],
    pair_distance: dict[float, ndarray],
    pair_distance_unit: PairDistanceUnit = METER,
)

Container holding relative (drift) pose deviations grouped by separation.

Relative deviations quantify drift between pose pairs separated by a certain spatial distance (meters) or temporal offset (seconds). Each key in the dictionaries corresponds to a separation value (bucket) and its list contains per-pair drift samples for that bucket.

Attributes:

  • pos_dev (Dict[float, ndarray]) –

    Mapping from pair distance to the position drift of each pair, relative to the pair distance: m/m for pairs by distance, m/s for pairs by time (RPEResult multiplies by drift_factor to show % and m/s).

  • rot_dev (Dict[float, ndarray]) –

    Mapping from pair distance to the orientation drift of each pair, relative to the pair distance: rad/m or rad/s.

  • pair_distance (Dict[float, ndarray]) –

    Raw separation measurements (meters or seconds) for each bucket, used for computing mean bucket spacing and step size.

  • pair_distance_unit (PairDistanceUnit) –

    Enumeration indicating whether bucket keys represent spatial separation (METER) or temporal separation (SECOND). Affects drift normalization and reporting units in RPEResult.

Examples:

import trajectopy as tpy reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj") estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj") rpe_dev = tpy.rpe(estimate, reference).rpe_dev distances = sorted(rpe_dev.pos_dev) # pair distances in meters tuple(float(distance) for distance in distances[:3]) (100.0, 200.0, 300.0) rpe_dev.num_pairs 32789

DeviationCorrelation(
    sampling_interval: float,
    num_samples: int,
    components: dict[str, ComponentCorrelation] = dict(),
    cross_correlation_directed: ndarray = (
        lambda: full((3, 3), nan)
    )(),
    cross_correlation_xyz: ndarray = (
        lambda: full((3, 3), nan)
    )(),
)

Temporal correlation of the deviations of an ATE result.

Deviations of trajectories (e.g. GNSS/INS) are usually correlated in time over seconds to minutes. Then, neighboring epochs do not provide independent information, and the number of independent deviations is much smaller than the number of epochs. The deviations are described as white noise (e.g. measurement noise of the reference) plus a correlated part, whose correlation time is given. Gaps (e.g. losses of a total station's lock) are respected: no deviation is correlated across a gap.

Attributes:

  • sampling_interval (float) –

    Typical time between the deviations [s].

  • num_samples (int) –

    Number of deviations.

  • components (dict[str, ComponentCorrelation]) –

    Correlation of each component (see COMPONENT_LABELS).

  • cross_correlation_directed (ndarray) –

    Correlation coefficients of along-track, horizontal and vertical cross-track at the same epochs (3x3).

  • cross_correlation_xyz (ndarray) –

    Correlation coefficients of x, y and z at the same epochs (3x3).

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> reference = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_gt.traj")
>>> estimate = tpy.Trajectory.from_file("./example_data/KITTI_ORB.traj")
>>> ate_result = tpy.ate(estimate, reference)
>>> correlation = ate_result.correlation
>>> sorted(correlation.components)[:3]
['along', 'cross_h', 'cross_v']

Analyzes the deviations of an ATE result in chronological order.

    Largest lag of the autocorrelation [s], at most n / 10 sampling intervals. Defaults to 600 s.

@classmethod
def from_ate_result(
    cls, ate_result: "ATEResult", *, max_lag: float = DEFAULT_MAX_LAG, window: float = DEFAULT_WINDOW
) -> "DeviationCorrelation":
    """Analyzes the deviations of an ATE result in chronological order.

    Args:
        ate_result (ATEResult): Result to analyze.
        max_lag (float, optional): Largest lag of the autocorrelation [s], at most n / 10 sampling
            intervals. Defaults to 600 s.
        window (float, optional): Length of the windows of the windowed standard deviations [s], at most a
            tenth of the duration (so that there are at least 10 windows). Defaults to 60 s.

    Returns:
        DeviationCorrelation: Correlation of every deviation component and the cross-correlations.
    """
    timestamps = ate_result.trajectory.timestamps
    if (duration := float(np.ptp(timestamps)) if len(timestamps) else 0.0) > 0:
        window = min(window, duration / MIN_WINDOWS)
    values = {
        "along": ate_result.pos_dev_along,
        "cross_h": ate_result.pos_dev_cross_h,
        "cross_v": ate_result.pos_dev_cross_v,
        "x": ate_result.pos_dev_x,
        "y": ate_result.pos_dev_y,
        "z": ate_result.pos_dev_z,
    }
    if ate_result.has_orientation:
        values |= {"roll": ate_result.rot_dev_x, "pitch": ate_result.rot_dev_y, "yaw": ate_result.rot_dev_z}

    step = sampling_interval(timestamps)
    correlation = cls(sampling_interval=step, num_samples=len(timestamps))
    # all components at once: the grid of the epochs and the pairs of each lag are the same
    lags, rho, pairs = autocorrelation(timestamps, np.column_stack(list(values.values())), max_lag=max_lag)
    for column, (name, component) in enumerate(values.items()):
        # white noise (e.g. of the reference) drops at once and would hide the correlated part
        correlated = white_noise_split(lags, rho[:, column], pairs)
        tau = correlation_time(lags, rho[:, column], level=correlated) if correlated > 0 else 0.0
        window_centers, window_std = windowed_std(timestamps, component, window)
        correlation.components[name] = ComponentCorrelation(
            lags=lags,
            autocorrelation=rho[:, column],
            pairs=pairs,
            white_noise_share=1.0 - correlated,
            correlation_time=tau,
            # the time covered by the deviations, without gaps
            effective_samples=effective_samples(len(component), len(component) * step, tau),
            std=float(np.std(component)) if len(component) else float("nan"),
            window_centers=window_centers,
            window_std=window_std,
        )

    correlation.cross_correlation_directed = _correlation_matrix(ate_result.abs_dev.directed_pos_dev)
    correlation.cross_correlation_xyz = _correlation_matrix(ate_result.abs_dev.pos_dev)
    return correlation

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy

Parameters of the spatio-temporal alignment of two trajectories.

The parameters of a similarity transformation (translation, rotation, scale), a time shift and a leverarm. Each is a Parameter with value, variance and whether it is estimated (enabled); disabled parameters keep their default value, which has no effect.

def get_covariance_matrix(self, *, enabled_only: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns the covariance matrix of the parameter set

    Args:
        enabled_only (bool, optional): If True, only the covariance matrix of the enabled parameters is returned. Defaults to True.

def validate_covariance(self) -> None:
    """Validates and normalizes the covariance matrix dimensions.

    Checks that the covariance matrix is square and matches either all parameters
    or only enabled parameters. Updates parameter variances from diagonal elements.

    Raises:
        AlignmentParametersError: If covariance matrix dimensions are invalid
    """
    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.covariance_matrix.shape[1]:
        raise AlignmentParametersError("Covariance matrix must be square.")

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] == len(self):
        self.variances = np.diag(self.covariance_matrix)
        return

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.num_enabled:
        raise AlignmentParametersError(
            "Covariance matrix must either be valid for all parameters or for all enabled parameters!"
        )

    covariance_matrix = np.zeros((len(self), len(self)), dtype=float)
    # for sub_row_indiex, full_row_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #     for sub_col_index, full_col_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #         covariance_matrix[full_row_index, full_col_index] = self.covariance_matrix[
    #             sub_row_indiex, sub_col_index
    #         ]
    covariance_matrix[np.ix_(self.enabled_indices, self.enabled_indices)] = self.covariance_matrix
    self.covariance_matrix = covariance_matrix
    self.variances_enabled = np.diag(self.get_covariance_matrix(enabled_only=True))

def to_dataframe(self) -> pd.DataFrame:

def validate_covariance(self) -> None:
    """Validates and normalizes the covariance matrix dimensions.

    Checks that the covariance matrix is square and matches either all parameters
    or only enabled parameters. Updates parameter variances from diagonal elements.

    Raises:
        AlignmentParametersError: If covariance matrix dimensions are invalid
    """
    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.covariance_matrix.shape[1]:
        raise AlignmentParametersError("Covariance matrix must be square.")

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] == len(self):
        self.variances = np.diag(self.covariance_matrix)
        return

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.num_enabled:
        raise AlignmentParametersError(
            "Covariance matrix must either be valid for all parameters or for all enabled parameters!"
        )

    covariance_matrix = np.zeros((len(self), len(self)), dtype=float)
    # for sub_row_indiex, full_row_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #     for sub_col_index, full_col_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #         covariance_matrix[full_row_index, full_col_index] = self.covariance_matrix[
    #             sub_row_indiex, sub_col_index
    #         ]
    covariance_matrix[np.ix_(self.enabled_indices, self.enabled_indices)] = self.covariance_matrix
    self.covariance_matrix = covariance_matrix
    self.variances_enabled = np.diag(self.get_covariance_matrix(enabled_only=True))

def apply_to(self, xyz: np.ndarray, quat_body: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Applies the leverarm to a set of positions using orientations

    Args:
        xyz (np.ndarray): Positions
        quat_body (np.ndarray): Orientations

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Leverarm applied positions
    """
    if len(xyz) != len(quat_body):
        raise ValueError("Dimension mismatch between positions and orientations.")

    xyz_red = np.zeros(xyz.shape)
    rot_matrices = Rotation.from_quat(quat_body).as_matrix()

    for i in range(len(xyz_red)):
        d_rot = rot_matrices[i] @ self.values
        xyz_red[i, :] = xyz[i, :] + d_rot

    return xyz_red

def validate_covariance(self) -> None:
    """Validates and normalizes the covariance matrix dimensions.

    Checks that the covariance matrix is square and matches either all parameters
    or only enabled parameters. Updates parameter variances from diagonal elements.

    Raises:
        AlignmentParametersError: If covariance matrix dimensions are invalid
    """
    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.covariance_matrix.shape[1]:
        raise AlignmentParametersError("Covariance matrix must be square.")

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] == len(self):
        self.variances = np.diag(self.covariance_matrix)
        return

    if self.covariance_matrix.shape[0] != self.num_enabled:
        raise AlignmentParametersError(
            "Covariance matrix must either be valid for all parameters or for all enabled parameters!"
        )

    covariance_matrix = np.zeros((len(self), len(self)), dtype=float)
    # for sub_row_indiex, full_row_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #     for sub_col_index, full_col_index in enumerate(self.enabled_indices):
    #         covariance_matrix[full_row_index, full_col_index] = self.covariance_matrix[
    #             sub_row_indiex, sub_col_index
    #         ]
    covariance_matrix[np.ix_(self.enabled_indices, self.enabled_indices)] = self.covariance_matrix
    self.covariance_matrix = covariance_matrix
    self.variances_enabled = np.diag(self.get_covariance_matrix(enabled_only=True))

Parameter(

    *,
    default: float = 0.0,
    enabled: bool = True,
    name: str = "",
    unit: Unit = NONE,

Class representing a stochastic parameter with variance.

A parameter holds a stochastic value with some variance and can be enabled or disabled. When disabled, the parameter's value equals its default value. The default value should be chosen so the parameter has no effect on computations (e.g., scale=1, rotation/translation=0).

Parameter disabling is used to exclude parameters from least-squares estimation during trajectory alignment.

Attributes:

  • default –

    Default value used when parameter is disabled

  • enabled –

    Whether the parameter is active

  • name –

    Parameter name for identification

  • unit –

    Unit of measurement for the parameter

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> scale = tpy.Parameter(value=1.0001, variance=1e-8, default=1.0, name="Scale")
>>> scale.disable()
>>> scale.value  # a disabled parameter has its default value
1.0

def __init__(
    self,
    value: float,
    variance: float = 0.0,
    *,
    default: float = 0.0,
    enabled: bool = True,
    name: str = "",
    unit: Unit = Unit.NONE,
) -> None:
    """Initializes a Parameter instance.

    Args:
        value: Initial parameter value
        variance: Initial parameter variance. Defaults to 0.0.
        default: Default value when disabled. Defaults to 0.0.
        enabled: Whether parameter is enabled. Defaults to True.
        name: Parameter name. Auto-generated if empty. Defaults to "".
        unit: Unit of measurement. Defaults to Unit.NONE.
    """
    self._value = value
    self._variance = variance
    self.default = default
    self.enabled = enabled
    self.name = name or f"Parameter {Parameter._cnt}"
    self.unit = unit

    Parameter._cnt += 1

def __str__(self) -> str:
    """Returns formatted string representation of the parameter.

    Returns:
        str: Formatted string with parameter name, value, unit, and standard deviation
    """
    formatter_value = UNIT_FORMAT_RULES.get(self.unit, {"normal": (1, "-", 4)})["normal"]
    formatter_variance = UNIT_FORMAT_RULES.get(self.unit, {"precise": (1, "-", 2)}).get("precise", formatter_value)
    # "-" for an invalid variance, e.g. of a parameter that the data does not determine
    std = (
        f"{np.sqrt(self.variance) * formatter_variance[0]:<8.{formatter_variance[2]}f}{formatter_variance[1]:<4}"
        if self.variance >= 0
        else f"{'-':<12}"
    )
    return f"{self.name:<16} = {self.value * formatter_value[0]:<8.{formatter_value[2]}f}{formatter_value[1]:<4}  s-dev.: {std}"

def __sub__(self, other: "Parameter") -> "Parameter":
    """Subtracts another parameter from this one.

    Args:
        other: Parameter to subtract

    Returns:
        Parameter: New parameter with subtracted value and combined variance

    # the variances of independent parameters add up, for differences as well as for sums
    return Parameter(
        value=self.value - other.value,
        variance=self.variance + other.variance,
    )

def update_from_dict(self, dct: dict) -> None:
    """Updates settings from a dictionary.

    Attributes missing from the dictionary keep their current value. Unknown attributes
    are ignored with a warning. The update is atomic: if any value is invalid, the
    settings remain unchanged.

    Args:
        dct: Dictionary containing updated settings data

    Raises:
        TypeError: If a value does not match the declared attribute type

    Examples:
        >>> import trajectopy as tpy
        >>> settings = tpy.MatchingSettings()
        >>> settings.update_from_dict({"max_time_diff": 0.05})
        >>> settings.max_time_diff
        0.05
    """
    updates = self._decoded_updates(dct)  # validates everything before anything is changed
    for attribute_name, value in updates.items():
        if isinstance(value, Settings):
            # update nested settings in place, so that references held elsewhere stay up to date
            getattr(self, attribute_name)._assign_from(value)
        else:
            setattr(self, attribute_name, value)

@classmethod
def from_bool_list(cls, bool_list: list[bool]) -> "AlignmentEstimationSettings":
    """Creates settings from a list of boolean values.

    Args:
        bool_list: 14 enable flags in the order translation x, y, z, rotation x, y, z, scale, time shift,
            lever arm x, y, z and sensor rotation x, y, z (the order of
            ``AlignmentParameters.enabled_bool_list`` followed by ``SensorRotationParameters.enabled_bool_list``).
            The sensor rotation is estimated if any of the last three is True.

    Returns:
        AlignmentEstimationSettings: New settings instance

    Raises:
        ValueError: If bool_list length is not 14
    """
    if len(bool_list) != 14:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Size mismatch: bool_list must have length 14 (Number of configurable parameters) (got {len(bool_list)})"
        )

    return AlignmentEstimationSettings(
        translation_x=bool_list[0],
        translation_y=bool_list[1],
        translation_z=bool_list[2],
        rotation_x=bool_list[3],
        rotation_y=bool_list[4],
        rotation_z=bool_list[5],
        scale=bool_list[6],
        time_shift=bool_list[7],
        leverarm_x=bool_list[8],
        leverarm_y=bool_list[9],
        leverarm_z=bool_list[10],
        sensor_rotation=any(bool_list[11:]),
    )

Bases: Settings

Configuration for alignment stochastic model (observation uncertainties).

Attributes:

  • std_xy_from (float) –

    Standard deviation of XY source position components in meters. Defaults to 1.0.

  • std_z_from (float) –

    Standard deviation of Z source position component in meters. Defaults to 1.0.

  • std_xy_to (float) –

    Standard deviation of XY target position components in meters. Defaults to 1.0.

  • std_z_to (float) –

    Standard deviation of Z target position component in meters. Defaults to 1.0.

  • std_roll_pitch (float) –

    Standard deviation of roll and pitch angles in radians. Defaults to ~0.017 rad (1°).

  • std_yaw (float) –

    Standard deviation of yaw angle in radians. Defaults to ~0.017 rad (1°).

  • std_speed (float) –

    Standard deviation of platform speed in meters per second. Defaults to 1.0.

  • error_probability (float) –

    Probability of error for stochastic testing. Defaults to 0.05.

  • variance_estimation (bool) –

    Enable a-posteriori variance factor estimation. Defaults to False.

  • robust_estimation (bool) –

    Down-weight epochs with large residuals (iteratively reweighted least squares with Huber weights), so that outliers, e.g. from wrong matches or GNSS multipath, hardly affect the estimated parameters. Defaults to True.

  • use_position_std (bool) –

    Weight the positions by the standard deviations stored with the trajectories (e.g. from the covariances of a ROS bag or the sx, sy, sz columns of a file) instead of the std_* values above, for each trajectory that has them. Defaults to True.

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> stochastics = tpy.AlignmentStochastics(std_xy_from=0.5, std_xy_to=0.02, std_z_to=0.05)

Bases: OptionEnum

Method for matching corresponding poses of two trajectories (see trajectopy.match_trajectories).

Each option can also be given as its value, e.g. method="nearest_temporal" (case-insensitive).

Attributes:

  • INTERPOLATION –

    "interpolation": the trajectory is interpolated at the timestamps of the reference; linearly for the positions, by SLERP for the orientations. The default.

  • NEAREST_TEMPORAL –

    "nearest_temporal": the pose with the nearest timestamp, within max_time_diff.

  • NEAREST_SPATIAL –

    "nearest_spatial": the nearest position, within max_distance; needs no common time reference.

  • NEAREST_SPATIAL_INTERPOLATED –

    "nearest_spatial_interpolated": the projection onto a line fitted through the k_nearest nearest positions of the reference.

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> tpy.MatchingMethod("Nearest_Temporal")
<MatchingMethod.NEAREST_TEMPORAL: 'nearest_temporal'>

Method for interpolating trajectories (see trajectopy.interpolate).

Each option can also be given as its value, e.g. method="linear" (case-insensitive).

Attributes:

  • LINEAR –

    "linear": linear interpolation of the positions, SLERP of the orientations.

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> tpy.InterpolationMethod("linear")
<InterpolationMethod.LINEAR: 'linear'>

docs.title: PairDistanceUnit
docs.text:
Bases: OptionEnum

Unit of the distances between the poses of the pairs of the relative pose error.

Each option can also be given as its value, e.g. pair_distance_unit="second" (case-insensitive). The aliases "m", "s" and "sec" are accepted, too.

Attributes:

  • METER –

    "meter": pairs of poses that are a given path length apart. The drift is given in % and rad/100 m.

  • SECOND –

    "second": pairs of poses that are a given time apart. The drift is given in m/s and rad/s.

Examples:

>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> tpy.PairDistanceUnit("m")
<PairDistanceUnit.METER: 'meter'>

Bases: OptionEnum

Order of the poses of a trajectory, which also defines its index (Trajectory.index).

Each option can also be given as its value, e.g. "time" (case-insensitive). The alias "arc_length" is accepted, too.

Attributes:

  • TIME –

  • PATH_LENGTH –

    "path_length": order along the path after spatial sorting (see trajectopy.sort_spatially); the index is the path length.

>>> tpy.Sorting("arc_length")

docs.title: Trajectory
docs.text:
Trajectory(
    positions: Positions | ArrayLike,
    rotations: Rotation | ArrayLike | None = None,
    timestamps: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    name: str = "",
    path_lengths: ndarray | None = None,
    velocity_xyz: ndarray | None = None,
    sorting: Sorting | str = TIME,
    position_std: ndarray | None = None,
)

Class representing a trajectory containing synchronized position, orientation, and time data.

Attributes:

  • positions (Positions) –

    Container for spatial coordinates and coordinate reference system (EPSG) data.

  • rotations (Rotation) –

    Container for orientation data (quaternions), or None if not provided.

  • timestamps (ndarray) –

    A 1D array of timestamps corresponding to each pose.

  • name (str) –

    An identifier string for the trajectory.

  • path_lengths (ndarray) –

    A 1D array of cumulative path lengths starting from zero.

  • sorting (Sorting) –

    The current sorting strategy (Sorting.TIME or Sorting.PATH_LENGTH).

  • position_std (ndarray | None) –

    Standard deviations of the positions along x, y and z in meters, shape (N, 3), or None if unknown. The alignment weights the positions by them.

See Also

trajectopy.Trajectory.from_file: loads a trajectory from a file.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import trajectopy as tpy
>>> timestamps = np.arange(0.0, 10.0, 0.1)
>>> xyz = np.column_stack([timestamps, np.sin(timestamps), np.zeros_like(timestamps)])
>>> trajectory = tpy.Trajectory(xyz, timestamps=timestamps, name="Curve")
>>> trajectory
<Trajectory 'Curve': 100 poses without orientations, ... m, EPSG 0, sorted by time>
>>> trajectory[10].timestamp
1.0
>>> len(trajectory[trajectory.timestamps >= 5.0])
50

Initialize a Trajectory object.

The poses are put into chronological order first; of poses with the same timestamp, only the first is kept (with a warning in the log). Then they are ordered according to sorting.

Parameters:

  • positions (Positions | ArrayLike) –

    Positions, either as a Positions container (which holds the EPSG code) or as an array of shape (N, 3) in a local frame (EPSG 0).

  • rotations (Rotation | ArrayLike | None, default: None ) –

    Orientations, either as Rotation or as an array of quaternions (x, y, z, w) of shape (N, 4). Defaults to None (no orientations).

  • timestamps (ArrayLike | None, default: None ) –

    Timestamps in seconds. If None, a range index is used.

  • name (str, default: '' ) –

    Name of the trajectory. Defaults to generic counter name.

  • path_lengths (Union[ndarray, None], default: None ) –

    Pre-calculated path lengths. If None or of the wrong length, they are computed from xyz.

  • velocity_xyz (Union[ndarray, None], default: None ) –

    Pre-calculated 3D velocities. If None or of the wrong length, they are computed from the positions and timestamps.

  • sorting (Sorting | str, default: TIME ) –

    Order of the poses, by time or by path length. Defaults to Sorting.TIME.

  • position_std (ndarray | None, default: None ) –

    Standard deviations of the positions along x, y and z in meters, shape (N, 3). Defaults to None (unknown).

Raises:

  • TrajectoryError –

    If the number of positions and rotations or timestamps do not match.
